question: Coverage is the bottleneck (69% -- each player still split across 20-30 threads). Pass 1 always compares a thread against a LONE FRAGMENT. Does a second, thread-to-thread pass close the gap?
pass2: greedy agglomeration over THREADS: repeatedly merge the best-scoring compatible pair (same team, non-overlapping spans), re-scoring after each round because every merge strengthens the surviving thread. Both sides carry accumulated evidence, which pass 1 never had.
protocol: 3-fold match rotation; calibrators, transition prior and fusion weights fitted on the other two matches. Pass-1 threshold fixed at 4.0; pass-2 threshold swept.
findings: The two-pass system DOMINATES the one-pass frontier. One pass at its aggressive setting gave 94.63% precision / 84.4% coverage; pass2@-2 gives 95.33% / 83.6% -- better precision at the same coverage. Lowering pass 1's threshold is a strictly worse way to buy coverage than adding pass 2.
At pass2@0 the trade is +10.0 points of coverage for -1.0 point of precision (69.0->79.1%, 97.65->96.63%), and threads per half roughly halve (778->426 on game_18_H1 against 23 true players).

Pass 2 is far more precise than pass 1 at the same threshold: at 4.0 it adds 146 correct merges for 6 wrong across all six halves. That is the accumulated-evidence effect appearing on BOTH sides of the comparison rather than one.
Pass-2 threshold is the better coverage dial. It can be lowered well below pass 1's because a thread-to-thread comparison has strictly more evidence than a thread-to-fragment one.
caveats: GT-substrate throughout: observability-span fragments, GT team gate, no fragment containing two players.
Fitting uses oracle threads on the other matches, so the fitted distribution is cleaner than the applied one.

Merge correctness is scored by majority player on each side, so an already-impure thread can absorb another and count as correct. Thread purity is reported alongside and falls at the lowest pass-2 threshold (92.6-80.9% at -2), which is the honest signal that -2 is past the useful point.
